$comment: The Taittirīya concept map, rendered by scripts/upanishads/build.mjs (editionMap). Boxes are 200×60 centred on x, y; mantras are anuvāka ids; study is a study id. Interpretive edges name whose interpretation they are.
intro: The three vallīs as a web of teachings, from the lesson on sound to the closing song. Solid lines follow the text’s own sequence and wording; dashed lines are interpretive links, each attributed.
desc: Fifteen teachings of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad across its three vallīs — instruction, the knowledge of Brahman and the five selves, and Bhṛgu’s inquiry — with the relations between them.

nodes.label: Prayer before learning
nodes.text: ‘May Mitra be kind to us … I shall speak the right, I shall speak the true.’ The prayer that opens the Śīkṣāvallī and, in the past tense, closes it.

nodes.label: The lesson on sound
nodes.text: Six things a reciter must get right: sound, accent, length, effort, evenness and joining.

nodes.label: The great joinings
nodes.text: The joining of two sounds becomes a way of looking at the worlds, the lights, learning, offspring and the self.

nodes.label: Mahaḥ, the fourth call
nodes.text: To bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ and suvaḥ the Upaniṣad adds a fourth, mahaḥ, and calls it Brahman; then the person in the space within the heart.

nodes.label: Om, the syllable
nodes.text: ‘Om is Brahman; Om is all this.’ The syllable of assent, of the chant and of the teacher’s beginning.

nodes.label: Study, teaching, conduct
nodes.text: Every duty is to be joined with study and teaching; the teacher’s last words to the departing student: speak the truth, practise dharma.

nodes.label: Truth, knowledge, infinite
nodes.text: ‘The knower of Brahman reaches the highest’, and Brahman is truth, knowledge, the infinite, hidden in the cave in the highest space.

nodes.label: Creation from the self
nodes.text: From the self, space; from space, wind; then fire, water, earth, plants, food, and the person made of the essence of food.

nodes.label: The five selves
nodes.text: Within the self made of food, a self made of breath; within that, of mind; then of understanding; then of bliss — each shaped like a bird.

nodes.label: The self made of bliss
nodes.text: The innermost of the five, with Brahman as its tail and foundation; the vallī’s great dispute is whether it is a product or the supreme self.

nodes.label: Raso vai saḥ: flavour
nodes.text: The self desired to be many, created and entered what it made; ‘he is flavour; obtaining flavour, one is glad’.

nodes.label: The measure of bliss
nodes.text: A ladder of bliss in steps of a hundred, from a happy human life to Brahman; and the verse ‘from which words turn back, with the mind’.

nodes.label: Bhṛgu’s tapas
nodes.text: Sent away with a definition instead of an answer, Bhṛgu finds Brahman by tapas, five times over: food, breath, mind, understanding, bliss.

nodes.label: Vows about food
nodes.text: Do not despise food, do not reject it, make much of it, turn no one away from your door; food and its eater rest in each other.

nodes.label: ‘I am food’: the song
nodes.text: Having passed through the five selves, the knower sits singing: ‘I am food, I am the eater of food, I am the maker of the verse.’

edges.label: then
edges.note: The prayer of 1.1 is followed by the lesson on sound in 1.2.

edges.label: joining of sounds
edges.note: 1.3 takes the joining (saṃhitā) of the lesson on sound and makes it a meditation.

edges.label: meditations
edges.note: The meditations continue: the teacher’s prayer (1.4), then the four calls (1.5–1.6).

edges.label: then Om
edges.note: After the fivefold world (1.7), 1.8 opens ‘om iti brahma’.

edges.label: study and teaching
edges.note: 1.9 joins svādhyāya and pravacana, study and teaching, to every other duty.

edges.label: to knowledge
edges.note: Śaṅkara (on 2.1): the first vallī gave meditations that do not conflict with rites; the second teaches the knowledge of Brahman. Kūranārāyaṇa (on 3.1) reads all three vallīs as one teaching of the Lord.

edges.label: Om is Brahman
edges.note: 1.8 names Om as Brahman; 2.1 defines Brahman.

edges.label: from that self
edges.note: 2.1: from that very self space came into being, and so on to the person.

edges.label: within the person
edges.note: 2.1–2.5: the person made of food, and the selves within it.

edges.label: is it Brahman?
edges.note: Śaṅkara (on 2.5): the self made of bliss is a product, with Brahman as its tail. Kūranārāyaṇa, Raṅgarāmānuja, Govindarāja and Rāmānanda: it is the supreme self. Madhva: Viṣṇu in each of the five.

edges.label: he is flavour
edges.note: 2.7: ‘he is flavour’ — the bliss the vallī has reached, named again.

edges.label: bliss measured
edges.note: 2.8 measures bliss, from a human being to Brahman.

edges.label: the same five
edges.note: The five answers are the five selves in order. Kūranārāyaṇa (on 3.1): the five meditations and the order of attainment in 3.10 are one order.

edges.label: food honoured
edges.note: Śaṅkara (on 3.7): food was the first door through which Brahman was known, so it is honoured like a teacher.

edges.label: I am food
edges.note: 3.10 ends the vows and meditations with the knower’s song.

edges.label: having reached
edges.note: 3.10.5: passing on to the self made of bliss, he sits singing this sāman.
